ny_9_basilisk.blurb: Basilisk is a compact wall of roughly fifty feet in the Powerlinez climbing zone, in the southwest corner of Harriman State Park, filed under Revolutionary Ramparts. It holds 19 routes, a mix of trad lines (11) and top-rope problems (8). Difficulty is broad: a few easy 5.6 and 5.7 outings, a solid core of 5.8 to 5.10, and a handful of 5.11 and 5.12 lines for stronger climbers. The face is steep and mostly vertical, so it suits people who want both gear practice and a hard top-rope session in one stop. Nearby low crags and boulders are located relative to this wall.

ny_devil_s_kitchen.blurb: Devil's Kitchen is a winter-only gully in Platte Clove, in the Catskills, where seeps freeze into pillars, corners and curtains. Of its 19 climbs, 17 are ice and 2 are mixed. The ice sits mostly at WI4, with a few easier WI3 lines and a pair of WI5s, and the mixed routes reach around M7. The hardest mixed terrain lies in the upper part of the gully. Expect cold, hard, brittle ice, and sun that changes the character of a route as the day moves on. Conditions depend on a sustained cold spell, so watch the temperature before committing.

ny_c_grease_gun_to_closure.blurb: This stretch of the Near Trapps, in the Gunks, lies beyond the Workout Wall and is almost entirely traditional climbing. Its 19 routes run from an easy 5.4 up to a 5.13 test piece, but most of the traffic is in the 5.6 to 5.10 range, with a good cluster of 5.10s and a few 5.7s. A trail follows the foot of the cliff, so moving between climbs is simple. Several lines are multi-pitch, and many have anchors that let a party step off after one or two pitches. It sits toward the quieter southern side of the Nears compared with the busy north end.

ny_khadejha_area.blurb: Khadejha Area is a small bouldering pocket on the left side of the West Cliff at Peterskill, in the Gunks region near Kerhonkson. The wall begins with a big roof high overhead, and the problems below it are mostly easy to moderate, from V0 to around V5, plus one very hard outlier. Alongside the ten boulder problems are a few short trad and top-rope lines. The cliff band here is mostly in shade, which keeps it cool on warm days but means holds can stay damp after rain. It is an easy first stop when walking along the cliff base.
ny_khadejha_area.approach: From the gatehouse, cross the open meadow toward the cliff, then follow the blue trail along the base for about two minutes.

_expect.name: N Country Rd Boulder (aka Billboard Rock)

ny_n_country_rd_boulder_aka_billboard_ro.blurb: A roadside boulder spot in Shoreham on Long Island, reached by a short walk from the nearby Split Rock trailhead. It carries 19 boulder problems with a wide spread: a few easy ones at V0 and V1, a middle band around V3 to V5, and a strong block of V6 to V8 lines, topped by one very hard low-start problem. Faces include a west face, a north slab and a west arete. It was revived recently, so expect some lichen and overgrowth on the holds. Long Island bouldering is small-scale rather than a destination, but this block gives real variety.

ny_north_face_of_pitchoff.blurb: The North Face of Pitchoff is a winter ice cliff in the Adirondacks above Keene Valley and Chapel Pond, off Old Mountain Road near Lake Placid. Its 19 routes are mostly ice, with two mixed lines. The ice is moderate: equal numbers of WI3 and WI4, a couple of WI5s, and a single WI6, while the mixed routes sit around M6 and M7. The cliff is high, quiet, remote and exposed, with sweeping views, and it can be bitterly cold early in the season. Facing north, it forms early and holds ice late, giving a long season.
ny_north_face_of_pitchoff.parking_note: Drive Old Mountain Road off Route 73 near Lake Placid to the small lot at the Jackrabbit ski trail trailhead; it holds only about six or seven cars.
ny_north_face_of_pitchoff.approach: Follow the Jackrabbit Ski Trail for 30 to 45 minutes; the cliff comes into view from the trail.

ny_witches_circle_the.blurb: The Witches' Circle is a patch of boulders gathered around a sundial, reached by a woodland trail in central New York. It has 19 boulder problems, nearly all easy to moderate: a handful of V0s, a big group at V1, several V2s, and a few harder problems up to about V5. The boulders offer overhangs and a few slab problems, with some landings that are sloped or have another boulder behind, so bring several pads. It is a short trip from the car and works well for a casual session or for newer boulderers.

ny_lake_pleasant_quarry.blurb: Lake Pleasant Quarry is a small abandoned quarry in the Indian Lake region of the Adirondacks. It has 19 short routes in the shade, mostly protected by trad gear, with about ten also bolted. The first several lines can be top-roped by reaching the anchors from above, while others need a rappel in. Grades run from beginner-friendly 5.3 through a lot of 5.6 to 5.9 climbing to a few 5.10s, so the place suits practice, instruction and groups. The base is flat and only a couple of minutes from the road, and it stays cool in summer.

_conflicts.ny_witches_circle_the: Stored rock is shale but the area page describes sandstone overhangs: https://mountainproject.com/area/117350794/the-witches-circle
